concepts.name: Asymptotic notation beyond big-O
concepts.gloss: Ω gives an asymptotic lower bound, Θ means both O and Ω, and o(f) means the ratio to f tends to zero, all stated for n large enough.

concepts.name: Logarithms, exponentials, floor and ceiling
concepts.gloss: The base-2 and natural logarithms as inverses of exponentials, their growth rates relative to powers of n, and rounding down or up to an integer.

concepts.name: Binary representation and bitwise operations
concepts.gloss: An integer written in a positional base as digits or bits with a most significant end, with addition by carries, bitwise XOR as addition mod 2, and signed words in two's complement.

concepts.name: Schoolbook integer arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Digit-by-digit addition, multiplication and division with remainder, with the quadratic cost of schoolbook multiplication on n-digit numbers.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on integers with equality taken up to multiples of a modulus, where the elements coprime to the modulus have multiplicative inverses.

concepts.name: Primes, coprimality and gcd
concepts.gloss: Primes and divisibility, greatest common divisors and Bezout coefficients via the extended Euclidean algorithm, and finding primes by trial division.

concepts.name: Sets, functions, Cartesian products and bijections
concepts.gloss: Finite sets and index ranges, tuples and Cartesian products, functions, bijections and their inverses, and lexicographic ordering of tuples.

concepts.name: Permutations
concepts.gloss: A bijection of a finite set onto itself, composed like functions, including swaps, cyclic shifts and permutation matrices.

concepts.name: Matrices and linear maps
concepts.gloss: Matrices acting on vectors as linear maps, with products, inverses, transposes, triangular and diagonal forms, and row reduction by Gaussian elimination.

concepts.name: Roots of unity
aliases: sum of roots of unity vanishes
geometric sum of roots of unity
concepts.gloss: The n complex solutions of z^n = 1, equally spaced on the unit circle, whose powers sum to zero unless the power is a multiple of n.

concepts.name: Summation, geometric series and products
concepts.gloss: Finite sums and products in sigma and pi notation, closed forms for geometric progressions, and telescoping cancellation.

concepts.name: Recursion and divide-and-conquer recurrences
concepts.gloss: Algorithms that call themselves on smaller inputs, with cost expressed by a recurrence such as T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n) and bounded by unrolling or the master theorem.

concepts.name: Worst-case running time and subroutines
concepts.gloss: A deterministic algorithm's cost is the maximum number of steps over inputs of a given size, and a reduction solves one problem by calling a procedure for another.

concepts.name: Triangle inequality and norms
concepts.gloss: The modulus of a sum is at most the sum of moduli, used to bound the size of sums and the accumulation of errors.

concepts.name: Rational numbers and rounding
concepts.gloss: Fractions with integer numerator and denominator, with rounding of a real number to the nearest integer or toward zero.

concepts.name: Newton's method
concepts.gloss: The iteration x ↦ x − f(x)/f'(x) for approximating a root, which roughly doubles the number of correct digits per step.

concepts.name: Tapes, scanning and sorting as basic machine procedures
concepts.gloss: Standard machine-level procedures such as one left-to-right scan, copying between tapes, and merging or sorting lists.

background.summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education: discrete mathematics (sets, functions, permutations, modular arithmetic, primes and gcd), calculus-level analysis (limits, sums, Newton's method), first-course linear algebra (matrices, inverses, Gaussian elimination, vectors) and complex numbers up to roots of unity, algorithm analysis (recursion, recurrences, big-O with its relatives Omega, Theta, little-o) and basic Turing machines. The reader knows binary representation and bitwise operations, and the textbook schoolbook multiplication. The reader has not studied abstract algebra beyond what the existing concepts introduce (rings and quotient rings, zero divisors, group characters), number-theory estimates on primes, numerical analysis of rounding errors, fast multiplication algorithms beyond the basics, or any coding-theory or quantum-computing notation, so those are explained in the wiki.
